context:
Goal: repos stay fast to download, and the automatic checks keep working.
Problem (money): GitHub refuses files over 100 MiB. Its large-file add-on (Git LFS) on a free or Pro plan gives 10 GiB of storage and 10 GiB of downloads a month, then stops, and every automatic check run spends download allowance.
Based on (read): GitHub's Git LFS billing page, read by the 3D tools survey lane.
Departs from: main — adds a rule for where 3D files are stored.

Not blocking: no repo stores 3D files yet.

options.gain: Code and the files a site ships stay together, and big source files use no GitHub allowance.
options.how: The small files a site actually uses go with the code; big working files go to a storage bucket.
options.label: Shipped files in Git LFS, source files in cloud storage
options.lose: Two places to look for files.

options.how: All 3D files go with the code.
options.label: Everything in Git LFS
options.lose: The allowance runs out; past it you pay $0.07 per GiB stored a month and $0.0875 per GiB downloaded.

options.how: No 3D files in git at all.
options.label: Everything in cloud storage
options.lose: Git keeps no history of file versions.

title: Where should big 3D files live?
why: Keeps what ships with the code, and keeps big files off the paid allowance.
